Sender displays an animated QR sequence; receiver points a camera at\n5\tthe sender's screen and decodes frames to reassemble the file.\n6\t\n7\tThis document covers **the receiving side only**: camera capture and QR decoding\n8\tin the browser.\n9\t\n10\t> **Empirical note.** Sections 3, 4 and 6 are not literature review. Treat absolute\n23\t> ms as indicative and **relative** differences between libraries as solid.\n24\t\n25\t---\n26\t## 1. Camera access (`getUserMedia`)\n27\t\n28\t> **Measured note.** Much of this section is **on-device measurement**, not spec\n29\t> reading: a **Pixel 6 running Chrome 150** (driven over ADB) and a Linux laptop\n30\t> running **Chromium 150 / Firefox 153**. Several widely repeated beliefs turned\n31\t> out to be false — they are called out inline. Chromium source citations are to\n32\t> `chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main`.\n33\t\n34\t### 1.1 What actually matters for scanning a screen at close range\n35\t\n36\tScanning an emissive display at 30–60 cm is a different problem from scanning a\n37\tprinted label. The target is **bright, high-contrast, self-illuminated, flat, and\n38\tchanging 15 times a second**. That inverts several defaults:\n39\t\n40\t| Concern | Printed label | Screen at close range |\n41\t|---|---|---|\n42\t| Illumination | often needs torch | **torch must be off** — specular glare |\n43\t| Focus | fixed/macro OK | **lock focus**; AF hunting is the top throughput killer |\n44\t| Exposure | longer is fine | **short exposure required** — target changes |\n45\t| Motion blur | hand shake only | hand shake **+ content changing mid-exposure** |\n46\t| Contrast | paper, ~4:1 | screen, very high — binarizer rarely the bottleneck |\n47\t| Resolution | more is better | **more is worse** — see §1.3; use zoom instead |\n48\t\n49\tThe two dominant real-world failures are **autofocus hunting** and — far less\n50\tobviously — **the camera silently delivering half the frame rate you asked for**\n51\t(§1.4). The second is the highest-value finding in this document after §4.\n52\t\n53\t### 1.2 Constraint reference and failure modes\n54\t\n55\t`MediaTrackConstraints` are specified in\n56\t[W3C Media Capture and Streams](https://www.w3.org/TR/mediacapture-streams/#media-track-constraints);\n57\tthe camera extensions (`focusMode`, `exposureMode`, `torch`, `zoom`,\n58\t`focusDistance`, `pointsOfInterest`) live in\n59\t[MediaStream Image Capture](https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-image/) and surface\n60\tthrough `track.getCapabilities()` / `applyConstraints()`.\n61\t\n62\t- `ideal` is a *preference* — never rejects.\n63\t- `exact` / `min` / `max` are *requirements* — reject with `OverconstrainedError`.\n64\t  This is the most common cause of \"works on my phone, not theirs\".\n65\t\n66\t**⚠️ Feature detection differs by engine — a successful `applyConstraints` proves\n67\tnothing.** Firefox **silently ignores** unknown constraints; Chrome **throws\n68\t`OverconstrainedError`**. So `try/catch` is not detection on Firefox. Likewise\n69\t`getSupportedConstraints().torch` returns `true` on desktop Chrome where no device\n70\thas a torch.\n71\t\n72\t> **Always gate on `track.getCapabilities()`, never on `getSupportedConstraints()`\n73\t> and never on a non-throwing `applyConstraints()`.**\n74\t\n75\tAlso note `resizeMode: 'none'` **bare is only an ideal**: Chromium 150 discarded it\n76\tand returned `crop-and-scale`; Firefox 153 threw on the same input. Use\n77\t`{exact:'none'}` if you mean it.\n78\t\n79\t### 1.3 Resolution — and why more is worse\n80\t\n81\t**Measured, Pixel 6, naive full-frame `drawImage` + `getImageData` scan loop:**\n82\t\n83\t| capture res | **scans/sec** | Chrome CPU (800% = 8 cores) | battery draw |\n84\t|---|---|---|---|\n85\t| 640×480 | **29.7** | 68 % | −140 mA |\n86\t| 1280×720 | **26.6** | 175 % | −575 mA |\n87\t| 1920×1080 | **11.9** | 188 % | −813 mA |\n88\t| 3840×2160 | **2.7** | 257 % | −1267 mA |\n89\t\n90\t**4K is disqualified** — under 3 scans/sec makes an animated-QR receiver unusable,\n91\tat 9× the battery draw of VGA. constructor(config: ReticleConfig) {\n    this.canvas = config.canvas;\n    this.video = config.video;\n\n    const ctx = this.canvas.getContext('2d');\n    if (!ctx) {\n      throw new Error('Failed to get 2D context for reticle canvas');\n    }\n    this.ctx = ctx;\n\n    this.criticalThreshold = config.criticalThreshold ?? this.CRITICAL_THRESHOLD;\n    this.warningThreshold = Update reticle state from decoded frame results\n   */\n  updateFromFrame(result: DecodedFrameResult): void {\n    const now = performance.now();\n    if (now - this.lastUpdate < this.updateInterval) {\n      return; // Throttle updates\n    }\n\n    this.lastUpdate = now;\n\n    // Extract metrics from diagnostics\n    const decodedTiles = result.diagnostics.filter(d => d.decoded && d.cameraPxPerModule);\n\n    if (decodedTiles.length === 0) {\n      this.state = {\n        ...this.state,\n        pxPerModule: 0,\n        quality: 'critical',\n        message: 'No QR codes detected - align screen within frame',\n      };\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Calculate average px/module across all detected tiles\n    const avgPxPerModule = decodedTiles.reduce(\n      (sum, tile) => sum + (tile.cameraPxPerModule || 0),\n      0\n    ) / decodedTiles.length;\n\n    // Determine quality category and message\n    let quality: ReticleState['quality'];\n    let message: string;\n\n    if (avgPxPerModule < this.criticalThreshold) {\n      quality = 'critical';\n      message = `TOO FAR: ${avgPxPerModule.toFixed(1)} px/module - Move closer`;\n    } else if (avgPxPerModule < this.warningThreshold) {\n      quality = 'warning';\n      message = `Adjusting: ${avgPxPerModule.toFixed(1)} px/module - Almost there`;\n    } else {\n      quality = 'good';\n      message = `Good: ${avgPxPerModule.toFixed(1)} px/module - Hold steady`;\n    }\n\n    // Extract all QR positions for visualization\n    const allPositions: Array<{ x: number; y: number }> = [];\n    for (const tile of decodedTiles) {\n      if (tile.position) {\n        allPositions.push(...tile.position);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Update frame dimensions from video\n    const frameWidth = this.video.videoWidth || 0;\n    const frameHeight = this.video.videoHeight || 0;\n\n    this.state = {\n      pxPerModule: avgPxPerModule,\n      quality,\n      message,\n      positions:     this.animationId = requestAnimationFrame(render);\n    };\n    render();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Stop the reticle animation loop\n   */\n  stop(): void {\n    if (this.animationId !== null) {\n      cancelAnimationFrame(this.animationId);\n      this.animationId = null;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Resize canvas to match video dimensions\n   */\n  private resizeCanvas(): void {\n    const rect = this.video.getBoundingClientRect();\n    this.canvas.width = rect.width;\n    this.canvas.height = rect.height;\n    this.canvas.style.width = `${rect.width}px`;\n    this.canvas.style.height = `${rect.height}px`;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Get quality color based on state\n   */\n  private getQualityColor(): string {\n    switch (this.state.quality) {\n      case 'good':\n        return '#4CAF50'; // Green\n      case 'warning':\n        return '#FF9800'; // Amber\n      case 'critical':\n        return '#F44336'; // Red\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Render the reticle overlay\n   */\n  private render(): void {\n    const { width, height } = this.canvas;\n\n    // Clear canvas\n    this.ctx.clearRect(0, 0, width, height);\n\n    // Draw reticle corner brackets\n    this.drawReticle(width, this.drawCoachingMessage(width, height);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Draw document-scanner-style reticle with corner brackets\n   */\n  private drawReticle(width: number, height: number): void {\n    const 'round';\n\n    // Top-left bracket\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(margin, margin + bracketLength);\n    ctx.lineTo(margin, margin);\n    ctx.lineTo(margin + bracketLength, margin);\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    // Top-right bracket\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(width - margin - bracketLength, margin);\n    ctx.lineTo(width - margin, margin);\n    ctx.lineTo(width - margin, margin + bracketLength);\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    // Bottom-right bracket\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(width - margin, height - margin - bracketLength);\n    ctx.lineTo(width - margin, height - margin);\n    ctx.lineTo(margin, height - margin);\n    ctx.lineTo(margin, height - margin - bracketLength);\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    // Draw center crosshair (subtle)\n    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3)';\n    ctx.lineWidth = 1;\n\n    const centerX = width / 2;\n    const centerY = height / 2;\n    const crossSize = 30;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(centerX - private drawQualityIndicator(width: number, height: number): void {\n    const ctx = this.ctx;\n    const x = 60;\n    const y = 60;\n    const radius = 25;\n\n    // Draw colored circle\n    ctx.fillStyle = this.getQualityColor();\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.arc(x, y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // Draw px/module text inside circle\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#000';\n    ctx.font = 'bold 14px system-ui';\n    ctx.textAlign = 'center';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n\n    const text = this.state.pxPerModule > 0\n      ? this.state.pxPerModule.toFixed(1)\n      : '---';\n\n    ctx.fillText(text, x, y);\n\n    // Draw \"px/module\" label below\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#fff';\n    ctx.font = '11px system-ui';\n    ctx.fillText('px/module', x, y + radius + 15);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Draw coaching message at bottom of screen\n   */\n  private drawCoachingMessage(width: number, height: number): void {\n    const ctx = this.ctx;\n    const padding = 20;\n    const fontSize = 16;\n    const lineHeight = 24;\n\n    ctx.font = `bold ${fontSize}px system-ui`;\n    ctx.textAlign = 'center';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'bottom';\n\n    // Measure text for background\n
